我非常能理解宝玉老师的这个感受，可以分享下我们目前的做法。

第一阶段，单bot模型单对话窗口。

直接使用一个bot对话窗口，让它24小时跑着，然后完成我们所有的任务。但是就会出现这个阶段遇到的问题，你不知道每个任务的进展和每个任务它对应的效果是怎么样。所以会出现一对一，然后你不知道情况的现象。

第二阶段，单bot模型多对话窗口。
我们会按照每一个任务作为一个项目，然后每个项目按照工作的节点去拆分成不同的 bot ，每个 bot 去执行相关的工作。保留一个bot，它会作为我们的中央大脑去安排每一个底下的 bot 去执行，并且去制定规则和标准。那这样的话，其实我们只需要跟主大脑去做对话，就能了解到整体的进展，并且可以制定一个整体的规则，不会乱。

那这个阶段最大的问题，还是你不知道每一个任务的具体进度，所以就到第三阶段。

第三阶段，单bot模型多对话窗口➕业务工作台。

我们会把整体这一套东西变成一个可视化的工作台。在这个工作台上面，可以看到每一个任务的进展，然后每一个项目的细节。如果出现了任何问题，你就可以及时地去做纠正，这里面会充杂着各种的业务节点的判断逻辑和预警逻辑。

目前我们第三阶段正在研发中。

quoted_tweet.text:
无论是 Grokbot / Dots 那样一个主会话，还是 Claude Code 那样一堆 Session 都是不够好的。

只有主会话意味着子任务你无法干预细节，无法像 Session 那样看到执行的细节，不方便去补充上下文和干预。

就好比你是老板，你给部门总监安排活，他们任务的执行情况对你是不透明的，你不能越过他们去看任务的执行情况和调整。

很多 Session 的问题在于管理起来很累，人需要自己去记住哪个 session 在干什么。就好比你直接管理所有项目，是每个项目的项目经理。

理想状况下，需要两者的结合：
人只要盯主对话，每次人往会话发消息的时候，会话的协调器决定你的消息是普通对话，还是说属于某个任务。

对于具体的任务，应该是能点开去干预的。

就好比你是一个老板，每一个 Bot/Channel 的主会话就相当于一个部门负责人，你只需要去和负责人打交道，负责人去派活，但是理想情况下你要能越过负责任去看任务细节，直接指挥。

24 小时在线的 AI Agent 助理，靠这五样东西

一直在线的 AI 助理，会盯邮件、等回复、到点提醒你。可它大部分时间其实在睡觉，不调用模型，也不花钱。

Anthropic 刚发文拆开讲了这种一直在线的 Agent：
一件事进了收件箱，它才醒过来跑一次；
定时器让它没人叫也能主动；
记忆文件夹让它醒来还记得你；
权限让它拿着你的账号也不乱来；
发件箱决定它什么时候开口。

这期一样一样讲清楚：它怎么醒、两件事同时来会不会打架、记忆为什么要省、要紧的事怎么等你拍板，以及为什么一开始最好让它安静一点。

来源
- Anthropic《Building always-on agents》（2026.11.13），作者 William Hu：https://claude.com/resources/articles/building-always-on-agents

@__oQuery 这一点你说的没问题，我不应该放在上面，不久后会删除。

像现在 Claude Code/Code 这样，你在做一件事之前，要先去创建/找 Project，然后再去开 Session，是很反人性的。

如果是写代码还好，但是普通任务还要这么搞是真的很烦。

相对来说 Bot 的形式肯定是更好的，我默认就有一个 Bot，还可以根据任务开不同的 Bot，只有一个主会话。

当我们觉得找 Sessions 很累时，说明我们不应该自己找，而是让 Agent 帮我们找（如图1）。

亲自去找，不管我们用无线画布、特殊标记还是任何方式，或许可以提高检索效率，足以管理十几个，但恐怕管理不了几十个，更不可能胜任几百个。

不仅找 Sessions 可以让 Agent 代劳，发送纠偏提示语也可以，复杂情况不要自己直接纠偏。就像不要自己写目标一样，而是跟一个临时 Sessions 结对探查其它 Sessions 的工作情况。

达成共识后，让该 Sessions 向一个或多个 Sessions 发送纠偏或引导提示语（如图2）。

我们可能可以亲自发引导提示语给10个会话，但很难做到准确发送给几十个，所以发送提示语本身也是应该 Agent 代劳的。

我们可以把这个模式称之为——Meta-Session，管理其它 Sessions 的 Session。它可以是临时的，也可以是持续的，但通常在我们授意下工作。

Yes, the green flame is caused by burning copper from depleting fuel in the regenerative cooling circuit and going oxygen-rich (closer to stoichiometric temperature) in the main combustion chamber. 

Slight underperformance of engines on this flight is the reason. The booster is meant to land with tiny residuals, so the solution is to improve engine performance and performance consistency (underway with Raptor V3.2), as well as adjust flight software to do MECO1 about one second earlier to ensure enough propellant for boostback and landing (tiny change).

These early ships and boosters are already outdated by improved designs in production or on the test stand, so this booster loss does not change our timeline to reach high volume, fully reusable Starship flights.

The Fable of Clawd

A 2 minute 4K film made entirely in Blender, from one prompt on Fable 5.2. It took about 4.5 hours.

Claude built every asset in Blender by writing Python:
- 5 characters and props: Clawd, his friend Pip, a toy truck, a 3D-printed tulip and a gift box
- 7 full sets: a study, a staircase, a street, a workshop, an airport, a night sky and a house
- every camera move and every frame of animation across 52 shots

That came to 12,500 lines of code. It started 7 copies of itself to build the sets at the same time.

Then it rented 89 GPUs through RunPod to render 3,220 frames as fast as possible, 36 of them running at once. Total cost: a little over $20.

My biggest takeaway is my Claude Code knows it has access to cloud compute, so it's much more ambitious.

I tried a similar prompt on my other computer that doesn't have the runpod skill setup and it wasn't nearly as high quality

text:
There is a part of the Ethereum space that's often pushed to the sidelines, yet refuses to disappear

@EFDevcon gave @sbetamc and me a stage to talk about the Iranian Ethereum community's journey over the past decade

These are all great questions, taking a quick stab: 

1/ More than off the table I'd say it's a distraction. ETH is a programmable store of value. And importantly Ethereum chooses security over zero issuance, and I think that's the correct choice. Bitcoin still needs to answer the question of what security will look like once block rewards are zero. Very unclear. 

@adietrichs and I gave a talk covering this point starting at 20:55: https://x.com/Bankless/status/1861121104884154600?a=dCg6s_lBBmQ5xuOIl_0&s=20

2/ I agree it needs to settle once and for all. I'd characterize Ethereum's philoshopy as "fastest viable ossificiation". Ethereum is playing a long-term game, and zooming out I strongly believe we'll be happy that Ethereum did not myopically ossify but is willing and able to converge on a policy that is fit for this civilizational foundation that we're all building. And importantly: Ethereum has only ever decreased its issuance and I consider this to be part of the social contract. 

3/ I think Ethereum is uniquely positioned to become the canonical root of trust for the world. Only Ethereum is credibly neutral and secure enough, and (!) set up architecturally for settling other chains. (Bitcoin is the former but not the latter). And I think of L2s as a critical piece in making this vision a reality: Ethereum as the root of trust but with activity that demands differentiation along dimensions that the L1 cannot offer (e.g. different configurations of speed, compliance, privacy) it can flow from Ethereum to L2s, while still inheriting the strongest guarantees that only Ethereum can offer. 

I spoke about this a lot in my recent talk at Devcon: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iPXY0oxjCRE

4/ This is a great question and I don't have an immediate answer, would love to hear your thoughts on this! :) 

5/ I strongly agree, and Ethereum is incredibly well positioned here. The EF has led the path with years of investments into post-quantum research, and Ethereum is now in this privileged position where we can accelerate timelines to be post-quantum and post-AI in 2027: https://x.com/ethlabs_org/status/2120621682889052345?a=tHgB7XnMjQgyRlwB2xY&s=20

And ETH will be a pqai store of value btw :)
